sentences.text:
1 The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act by claiming compensation for the injuries are sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 03-01-2024.
2.

The petition averments in brief are as under:
On 03-01-2024 at about 12.00 a.m.,the petitioner was proceeding by riding the motor cycle bearing No. KA.50.W.3997 along with one pillion rider from Kothanur towards Thanisandra on the extreme left side on Thanisandra service road and when he reached near Saamar International School, Bengaluru, at that time the driver of the Cab bearing No. KA.05.AJ.8953 came from opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner, came to his extreme right side ie., wrong side and dashed against the motor cycle of the petitioner and caused the accident.
As a result, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Hosmat hospital,
wherein he was diagnosed, took treatment and discharged with an advice of regular followup treatment and bed rest.
Petitioner has spent a sum of Rs.1,20,000/- towards medical expenses, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges.

Prior to the accident, petitioner was very hale and healthy, aged about 23 years and working as technical content intern (SME) Data Science at Incanus Technologies Private Limited and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries petitioner is not able to do his work as he was doing prior to the said accident and suffered loss of income.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Hence, prays to award compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest.
3.
After service of notices, both the respondents appeared through their respective counsels but the 1st respondent - owner has not filed written statement.

Respondent No.2 - insurance company has filed its written statement by admitting the issuance of policy to the Car bearing No. KA.05.AJ.8953 and the liability of this respondent is any is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy and the policy was valid at the time of accident.
Further it has denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner.

Further it has contended that, the respondent No.1 owner has entrusted the vehicle to the person who was not having valid driving license and the vehicle was not having valid permit and fitness as on the time of accident and hence violated the policy conditions.

It has further denied the cause and manner of accident and contended that the petitioner without wearing helmet has ridden the third party motor cycle in a rash and negligent manner and without having valid DL caused the accident.
Further contended that, there is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the claim petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous in- juries due to the actionable negligent riding of motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA.50.W.3997 by its rider, in RTA took place on 03-01-2024 at about 12.00 a.m., on Thanisandra ser- vice road, Near Saamar International School, Bengaluru?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, what amount and from whom?
3.

What Order or Award?
5.
In order to prove the claim petition, the petitioner examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to 14.
Further, examined the Dr. Nagaraj B N, Orthopaedic surgeon at SOADS hospital as PW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P.15 & 16.

On the other hand, the director talent acquisition at Incanus Technologies Pvt Ltd., is examined as RW.1 and got marked Ex.R1 and the driver of the offending car is examined as Rw.2.
6.
Heard the arguments of both sides and perused the material evidence that are available on record.

At the time of arguments it is found that issue No.1 was wrongly framed by putting the burden to prove the negligence of the rider of motor cycle bearing No.KA.50.W.3997 but the pleadings and the available records alleges the negligence of driver of Cab bearing No. KA.05.AJ.8953.

Hence the issue No.1 is recasted as follows:
Recasted issue No.1:
Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligent driving of Cab bearing No. KA.05.AJ.8953 by its driver, in RTA took place on 03-01-2024 at about 12.00 a.m., on Thanisandra service road, Near Saamar International School, Bengaluru?
7.

That by reiterating all the averments made in the petition, the petitioner has filed his affidavit in lieu of- examination in-chief, which is considered as P.W.1.

In support of his case, he has produced certified copies of FIR, complaint, spot mahazar along with sketch, wound certificate, police intimation and charge sheet, which are marked under Ex.P.1 to 7.
9.
On perusal of Ex.P1- FIR which is registered on the basis of Ex.P2 first information given by one Mohammad Siddique who is the father of the petitioner.
Thereafter the spot mahazar and sketch as per Ex.P3 & 4 were conducted by the IO wherein it discloses that the accident spot is in the service road.

It is found that the driver of Cab bearing No. KA.05.AJ.8953 while entering in to the service road dashed against the motor cycle of the petitioner who was coming in the left side portion of the service road.
Further the Ex.P9 is the IMV report.
On perusal of the same it is clear that the accident is not due to any mechanical defect of the vehicles and both the vehicles were got damaged in its front portion.
The Cab bearing No. KA.05.AJ.8953 has got damages in its front left side bumper and front left side head light cover.
Further the motor cycle of the petitioner has got damages in its left side body.
This shows that the front portion of the Cab bearing No. KA.05.AJ.8953 has dashed against the motor cycle of the petitioner.

Thus, it evidentiates that the driver of the Cab bearing No.
KA.05.AJ.8953 was negligent and has entered into the service road in rash and negligent manner thereby dashed against the motor cycle of the petitioner.

Even though the learned counsel for respondent No.2 insurance company cross-examined the petitioner about his negligence, the contents of Ex.P3 mahazar, Ex.P4 rough sketch and Ex.P9 IMV report falsifies the contention of contributory negligence of the petitioner.

Thus, the documents Ex.P3 mahazar, Ex.P4 rough sketch and Ex.P9 IMV report establishes the negligence of driver of the Cab bearing No. KA.05.AJ.8953.
10.

Further the charge sheet as per Ex.P7 is filed against the driver of Cab bearing No.
KA.05.AJ.8953 for the offences punishable U/Sec.279 and 338 of IPC wherein the IO after detailed investigation opined that the accident was caused by the negligence of driver of Cab bearing No.
KA.05.AJ.8953, accordingly he was charge sheeted.

The view taken by this Court that the police records are prima- facie proof in support of the case of the petitioner, is supported by the decision rendered in Kishan Gopal and another Vs. Lala and others reported in 2013 (4) T.A.C 5 (S.C.),
wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has categorically held thus:
In view of the aforesaid facts, the Tribunal should have considered both oral and documentary evidence referred to supra and appreciated the same in the proper perspective and recorded the finding on the contentious issue No. 1 & 2 in the affirmative.

Rule 8 of the Rules of the Road Regulations 1989 reads as follows:
Caution at road junction: The driver of a motor vehicle shall slow down when approaching at a road intersection, a road junction, pedestrian crossing or a road corner, and shall not enter any such intersection, junction or crossing until he has become aware that he may do so without endangering the safety of persons thereon.
It is very clear from the above Rule that the driver of the motor vehicle shall slow down the vehicle when he is approaching at a road intersection, junction, road corner.

Rule 12 of the Rules of the Road Regulations 1989 reads as follows:
Taking U' turn.
No driver shall take a U' turn where U' turn is specially prohibited and on busy traffic road.
If a U' turn is allowed the driver shall show signal by hand as for a right turn, watch in the rear view mirror and turn when safe to do so.
It is very clear from the above said rule that if a driver is allowed to take U turn, he has to show signal by hand and watch on both sides of the road and cautiously take turn.

11. It is very clear from the evidence of the parties and spot mahazar, spot sketch,
IMV report,the driver of the car was proceeding at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and has not made any effort to slow down the car.

Even the deceased was taking U turn without following the rules and vehicles proceedings on National Highway and negligently took U-turn to go to the other side of the road to fill petrol in the petrol bunk.

From the above discussions and considering the oral evidence of the parties and materials available on record such as spot sketch, mahazar and IMV report, I am of the considered opinion that both the driver of the cab as well as deceased have equally contributed to the accident to the extent of 50% each.
12.
In the present case on hand, the accident spot is near to the space available to enter into the service road.
As such, by relying on the above quoted judgment the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 insurance company argued to consider the contributory negligence.
But in the present case the offending cab was entering into the service road from main road.

The damages Mohammed Sufiyan vs Raju C on 5 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133237852/
5 mentioned in Ex.P9 IMV report shows that the front headlight area of the offending cab has got damages.
Thus, it is evident that the driver of the offending car has entered into the service road in a rash and negligent manner whereas, the petitioner was coming in the left side portion of the road.
This shows that the driver of the cab was negligent.

Thus, the IMV report and rough sketch establishes the negligence of the driver of the cab and no grounds are made out to consider the contributory negligence as such, in my humble opinion the above quoted judgment relied by the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 is not applicable to the case on hand.
13. Further the RW.2 the driver of the offending cab bearing No. KA-05-AJ-8953 examined as RW.2 who deposed by alleging the negligence of the petitioner.
But the mahazar and IMV report depicts the negligence of the RW.2- driver.
Thereby the evidence of RW.2 failed to establish the negligence or the contributory negligence of the petitioner.

14. It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the inc ident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.

Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

sentences.text: The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

Further the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105,
where the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka considering the fact that the rider of the offending vehicle was not examined to prove any contributory negligence on the part of scooterist held that the accident had occurred due to rash or negligent driving by the rider of the offending van.

15. In view of the ratio laid down in the authorities referred to above and applying the settled principle of law to the case at hand, which is further supported by the oral and documentary evidence adduced by PW-1, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the accident leading to this case indeed occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the Cab bearing No.
KA.05.AJ.8953 resulting in petitioner sustaining injuries.
Thus, the allegation of driver of the Cab bearing No. KA.05.AJ.8953 driving his car in rash and negligent manner stands established.
Accordingly, issue No.1 answered in the affirmative.

16.

Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.

sentences.text: At the time of alleged accident the petitioner was aged about 23 years.
Aadhaar card produced at Ex.P13 shows the date of birth of the petitioner as 07-05-2001, the accident was occurred on 03-01-2024, as on the date of accident petitioner was aged about 23 years.
In the petition itself he has averred that immediately after the accident he was shifted to Hosmat hospital, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient.
As per the discharge summary marked at Ex.P8 the petitioner was admitted to Hosmat hospital as an inpatient from 03-01-2024 to 04-01-2024 and sustained right knee CLW with quadriceps tendon injury.

As per Ex.P5 wound certificate, the petitioner sustained following injuries:
RIGHT KNEE 1.

2. Subcutaneous tissue and tendon exposed 3.

All the said injuries are grievous in nature.
By considering the nature of the injuries and the period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident Rs.60,000/- may be awarded to the petitioner under this head.
b) Medical expenses: The petitioner has produced medical bills as per Ex.P11, amounting to Rs.1,07,215/- which are supported by medical prescriptions marked at Ex.P10.
The medical bills are not seriously disputed by the respondents and no grounds are made out to disbelieving these bills.

Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case in combined with the alleged injuries the petitioner is entitled for the reimbursement of the same by rounding of the same i.e., Rs.1,07,300/-.
c) Loss of income during laid up period:
The petitioner has stated that he was working as technical content intern (SME) data science at Incanus Technologies Pvt Ltd and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.
To prove the said fact, the petitioner has produced account statement marked at Ex.P14.

The Ex.P14 discloses that on 6.11.2023 Rs.13,427/- was credited to the account of the petitioner by Incanus Technologies Pvt. Further the respondent No.2 also summoned the employer and examined the RW.1 Bharath Bhartia who is the Director of Talent Acquisition in Incanus Technologies Pvt. Ltd., who produced the salary slips.

In the said salary slips it discloses that the total earning of the petitioner in In the month of October, 2023 Rs.13,427/-, in November 2023 was Rs.29,097/ and in the month of December it was Rs.23,500/- and in the January it was only Rs.1,290/-.

In this regard in his oral evidence the RW.1 deposed that the petitioner joined their Mohammed Sufiyan vs Raju C on 5 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133237852/
7 company on 6.10.2023 i.e., in the month of October 2023 and initial 3 months will be the internship for their employees if their performance was good they will be considered as permanent employees.
The date of accident is 3.1.2024.
After the accident the petitioner had not been to the work.

The evidence marked at Ex.P14 account statement and the evidence of RW.1 which is summoned by the respondent No.2 insurance company establishes that the prior to the accident the petitioner earned in the month of November 2023 was Rs.29,097/ and in the month of December it was Rs.23,500/-.
Due to the accident he was not able to earn from the month of January.
Thereby, the income of the petitioner is established as Rs.29,097/- p.m.
The PW.2 doctor who assessed the disability of the petitioner in his cross-examination stated that for the injuries sustained by the petitioner the normal duration for healing is 4 months.
No grounds are made out to disbelieve the said contention.
The injuries sustained by the petitioner required bed rest and also need to be healed before joining to works.

The evidence of the RW.1 evidentiates that from January the petitioner had not been to his work as such, by considering the healing period of 4 months, the petitioner is entitled for the compensation during the said four months.
As per the discharge summary marked at Ex.8 the petitioner was admitted to Hosmat Hospital for 2 days.
Thereafter usually the healing period has to be considered.

As such by relying on the answers given by PW.2 doctor at the time of cross-examination in this regard, this court is of the opinion that in total 4 months period including 2 days inpatient period may be considered under this head as a loss of income.

So, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.29,097 X 4 months =
Rs.1,16,388/- during the laid up period.

d) Disability;- To prove the nature of injuries sustained by him the petitioner has examined Dr.Nagaraj B N, Orthopaedic Surgeon at SOADS Hospital as PW.2 and through him clinical notes and X-ray were got marked at Ex.P15 & 16.
According to the evidence of this witness the petitioner sustained right knee cut lacerated wound with quadriceps tendon injury.
He has examined the petitioner for assessment of disability and the petitioner has suffered total disability of 40% at right lower limb and whole body at 13%.

When the PW.2 cross-examined he has stated that the quadriceps loss and wastage of muscle can be regained through physiotherapy and as the petitioner is aged less than 25 years, comparing to other aged patients the healing process of the petitioner is good and there is no complication and also there is no bone injury to the petitioner.

Thereby by keeping the answers given by the PW.2 in the cross-examination it is necessary to verify whether after the healing period when the loss of quadriceps and wastage of muscle can be regained through physiotherapy whether the petitioner has really has permanent disabilities which effects his occupation or not has to be looked into.

sentences.text: By relying on the above quoted judgments, the learned counsel for the respondent no.2 insurance company argued that in this case, no future loss of income is awarded.
No doubt that the PW.2 doctor examined the petitioner and assessed the physical disability.
As per the evidence of Pw.2 doctor the petitioner has sustained right knee cut lacerated wound and quadriceps tendon injury.
As per the evidence of PW.2 as admitted in the cross-examination the loss of quadriceps can be regained through physiotherapy.
In this case, as stated by the petitioner he was working as Technical Content Inturn (SME) Data Science at Incanus Technologies Pvt. Ltd.,
The evidence of RW.1 reveals that neither they have removed the petitioner nor the petitioner has given resignation letter or the medical documents by leaving the job.
The nature of the job of the petitioner is not affected by the injuries sustained by the petitioner in RTA.
The injury of loss of quadriceps will not effect the way of occupation or nature of the work of the petitioner.
As admitted by the PW.2 doctor the petitioner is of young age and the loss of quadriceps is regained by the petitioner by physiotherapy and the wounds are healed.
Thereby there is no specific evidence to s how that due to the injury of right knee cut lacerated wound and quadriceps tendon injury the petitioner was unable to attend his work after the recovery.

As admitted by the PW.2 doctor the healing period was four months and after the said four months, no evidence is available to hold that due to the said injury the petitioner has lost his working capacity.
Thereby the petitioner in the absence of specific medical evidence not entitled for the compensation under this head.
e) FOOD, NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE;

As per wound certificate marked at Ex.P5 the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
By considering the nature of the injury and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident.

f) ATTENDANT CHARGES:
The petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the accident.
The petitioner has spent 2 days in the hospital and there is no evidence or pleading in this regard to show that the petitioner is in need of attendant.

But by considering the nature of the fracture as discussed above, it may be considered to award attendant charges at Rs.1,000/- per day i.e.,
Rs.2,000/- in total as the petitioner has spent 2 days in the hospital.

g) Towards loss of amenities and enjoyment of life:
The petitioner admitted to the hospital for the injuries sustained by him, which might certainly have deprived him of the basic comforts and enjoyment.
The evidence of Pw2 doctor reveals that there is a restriction of movements and also physical disability to some extent in mobility and stability components.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award a reasonable sum of Rs.40,000/- under this head.
Future medical expenses: NIL

Hence, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner and the respondent No.2 insurance company shall indemnify the compensation on behalf of the respondent No.1 owner.

opennyai_summary.arguments:
The view taken by this Court that the police records are prima- facie proof in support of the case of the petitioner, is supported by the decision rendered in Kishan Gopal and another Vs. Lala and others reported in 2013 (4) T.A.C 5 (S.C.),
wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has categorically held thus:
In view of the aforesaid facts, the Tribunal should have considered both oral and documentary evidence referred to supra and appreciated the same in the proper perspective and recorded the finding on the contentious issue No. 1 & 2 in the affirmative.
The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 insurance company relied on the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA No.
1205-2021 connected with MFA No. 1803-2021 between HDFC Ergo Gen. Ins. Co,
Ltd., V/s. Hanumanthappa and Others, wherein it held as follows;

It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the inc ident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.
The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
By relying on the above quoted judgments, the learned counsel for the respondent no.2 insurance company argued that in this case, no future loss of income is awarded.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
But it has recorded the finding in the negative on the above issues by adverting to certain statements of evidence of AW-1 and referring to certain alleged discrepancies in the FIR without appreciating entire evidence of AW-1 and AW-2 on record properly and also not assigned valid reasons in not accepting their testimony.
The Tribunal should have taken into consideration the pleadings of the parties and legal evidence on record in its entirety and held that the accident took place on 19.07.1992, due to which Tikaram sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the same and the case was registered by the Uniara Police Station under Sections 279 and 304-A, IPC read with Sections 133 and 181 of the M.V. Act against the first and second respondents.

4 respondent Nos.1 & 2 are not in dispute, therefore, the Tribunal should have no option but to accept the entire evidence on record and recorded the finding on the contentious issue Nos.1 and 2 in favour of the appellants.
It is very clear from the above Rule that the driver of the motor vehicle shall slow down the vehicle when he is approaching at a road intersection, junction, road corner.
11. It is very clear from the evidence of the parties and spot mahazar, spot sketch,
IMV report,the driver of the car was proceeding at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and has not made any effort to slow down the car.
Even the deceased was taking U turn without following the rules and vehicles proceedings on National Highway and negligently took U-turn to go to the other side of the road to fill petrol in the petrol bunk.
In the present case on hand, the accident spot is near to the space available to enter into the service road.
But in the present case the offending cab was entering into the service road from main road.
Thereby the evidence of RW.2 failed to establish the negligence or the contributory negligence of the petitioner.
Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.
Thus, the allegation of driver of the Cab bearing No. KA.05.AJ.8953 driving his car in rash and negligent manner stands established.
In the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA No. 5905-2006 between Oriental Ins.
Co. Ltd., V/s. Shivanna and another, the Hon'ble High Court when the false certificate is given by the doctors while assessing the disability has to be rejected and proper investigation has to be done by the investigating agency in respect of the accident.
In the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka 1449-2023 connected with 3330-2023 between Iffco Tokio Gen. Ins. Co. ltd., V/s. Smt. Jayashree and another, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has held that when there is no exact evidence to show that due to the injuries the petitioner has lost working capacity, the consideration of loss of future income due to disability does not arise.
No doubt that the PW.2 doctor examined the petitioner and assessed the physical disability.
As per the evidence of Pw.2 doctor the petitioner has sustained right knee cut lacerated wound and quadriceps tendon injury.
As per the evidence of PW.2 as admitted in the cross-examination the loss of quadriceps can be regained through physiotherapy.
The evidence of RW.1 reveals that neither they have removed the petitioner nor the petitioner has given resignation letter or the medical documents by leaving the job.
The nature of the job of the petitioner is not affected by the injuries sustained by the petitioner in RTA.
The injury of loss of quadriceps will not effect the way of occupation or nature of the work of the petitioner.
As admitted by the PW.2 doctor the petitioner is of young age and the loss of quadriceps is regained by the petitioner by physiotherapy and the wounds are healed.
Thereby there is no specific evidence to s how that due to the injury of right knee cut lacerated wound and quadriceps tendon injury the petitioner was unable to attend his work after the recovery.
As admitted by the PW.2 doctor the healing period was four months and after the said four months, no evidence is available to hold that due to the said injury the petitioner has lost his working capacity.
Thereby the petitioner in the absence of specific medical evidence not entitled for the compensation under this head.
By considering the nature of the injury and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident.

Therefore, it is just and proper to award a reasonable sum of Rs.40,000/- under this head.
Future medical expenses: NIL
Thus, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
a. Towards pain and agony Rs. 60,000/- b.
Towards medical expenses Rs. 1,07,300/-
c.
Towards loss of income during Rs. 1,16,388/-
 laid up period d.
Towards disability NIL e. Towards food, nourishment and Rs. 30,000/-
 conveyance f.
Towards attendant charges Rs. 2,000/-
g. Towards loss of amenities Rs. 40,000/-
h.
Towards future medical expenses NIL
No other grounds are made out by showing the violation of policy condition by the respondent No.1 owner.
Hence, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner and the respondent No.2 insurance company shall indemnify the compensation on behalf of the respondent No.1 owner.
The petitioner is entitle for compensation with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
Accordingly, this issue answered in the affirmative.
For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.3,55,688/-
(Rupees Three lakhs fifty five thousand six hundred eighty eight only) with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a., from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The respondent No.2 insurance company is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
Considering the quantum of amount awarded to petitioner, it is ordered to release the entire amount in his favour.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw up award accordingly.
